match_note: Referee 1 calls this a 'Third report', so earlier review rounds are not in the file and the 'first round' here is a late-stage revision. The reviewed manuscript has a drift-diffusive Eq. (3), 'anomalously high IX mobility' wording, and the title 'Efficient transport kinetics of indirect excitons...'; v1 has only diffusive (Eq. 1) and ballistic (Eq. 2) models, speaks of anomalously high diffusivity and agreement with ballistic transport, and has a different title. The density estimate (n ~ 2e11 cm^-2, N ~ 1/2) and Bose-Hubbard comparison are in v1.

concerns.quote: the revised analysis does not uniquely distinguish ballistic or superfluid transport from drift-driven or interaction-induced expansion
concerns.summary: Rapid IX cloud expansion could be drift- or interaction-driven, so superfluidity should be toned down to one possible explanation.

concerns.quote: superfluidity means that the mobility is infinite, rather than merely finite and large
concerns.summary: Framing via 'high mobility' from a drift-diffusion equation is misleading for a superfluid; a two-fluid hydrodynamic model would be needed, so the wording should change.

concerns.quote: whether it relates to Bose-Hubbard physics in a moire system or to the physics of the Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless transition
concerns.summary: Unclear whether the superfluid scenario is moire Bose-Hubbard or BKT in a disorder-free 2D sample; left open by the referee.

concerns.quote: The main text should include the density-calibration procedure, the assumptions used to convert the measured energy shift into exciton density
concerns.summary: The power-to-density-to-filling calibration and its uncertainties, central to the Bose-Hubbard comparison, belong in the main text.
